slides.headline: Wide Views, Brief Flights
slides.subheadline: The flight-time claim depends on battery condition and controlled testing.

items.title: Camera
items.body: 2K video, 148-degree field of view and 360-degree camera rotation.

items.title: Flight time
items.body: 8 minutes on a new, fully-charged battery under controlled conditions.

items.title: Low-light illumination
items.body: Two LED lights activate in low-light conditions.

slides.svgBlueprint: Center a schematic camera with a mathematically accurate 148-degree field-of-view wedge and a separate circular arrow for 360-degree camera rotation. Place the camera caption above, the complete flight-time qualification below, and the LED caption beside two light marks. Use an unscaled battery outline, not a percentage gauge. Do not imply 360-degree simultaneous capture.

slides.headline: Autonomy Has Conditions
slides.subheadline: Scheduled patrols require a subscription; certain surfaces may degrade navigation.

items.title: Subscription gate
items.body: Set routes and schedules require an Amazon Ring Protect subscription.

items.title: Reflective surfaces
items.body: Polished marble or wet tile may degrade drone navigation.

items.title: Blank or transparent surfaces
items.body: Featureless blank matte walls, frameless glass and mirrors may degrade navigation.

slides.svgBlueprint: Run one illustrative diagonal drone route through the slide. Attach exactly three numbered margin notes: a subscription gate, a reflective floor patch, and a blank-wall/glass boundary. Change the route from solid to dashed near challenging surfaces to indicate possible degradation, not certain failure. Keep all explanatory copy outside the route corridor.

slides.subheadline: An adjustable mast supports views over counters, shelving and other obstacles.

items.title: Video
items.body: Livestreams and records in up to 4K.

items.title: Stationary scan
items.body: Can perform a 360-degree scan at a designated location.

items.title: Claimed coverage

slides.headline: Your Floors Set The Boundaries
slides.subheadline: The rover’s operating limits are physical, not just digital.

items.title: Indoor, single-floor operation
items.body: The rover cannot climb stairs.

items.title: Incompatible terrain
items.body: Curved edges, sunken areas and black glossy floors are incompatible.

items.title: Flooring transitions
items.body: Transitions greater than 1.375 inches (3.5 centimeters) are incompatible.

slides.svgBlueprint: Use one continuous architectural cross-section with three annotated zones: stairs, a grouped terrain vignette, and a raised flooring transition. Put the exact transition threshold beside a dimension bracket. Mark incompatible features with simple accent slashes. State that the drawing is schematic; do not imply transitions at or below the threshold are universally supported.

slides.headline: Encryption Does Not End The Debate
slides.subheadline: Amazon promises protection; the EFF disputes how far it goes.

items.title: Amazon’s promise
items.body: Both devices: Throw Away the Key Encryption, introduced September 2026.

items.title: EFF’s assessment
items.body: The protection remains well short of end-to-end encryption.

items.title: Rover cloud retention
items.body: Doorbell rings, motion, Live View: videos stored for up to 180 days.

slides.svgBlueprint: Build three vertically separated editorial tiers: Amazon’s stated encryption protection, the EFF’s assessment, and Rover cloud retention. Use an outlined shield, a qualification bracket, and a cloud/archive icon respectively. These are explanatory symbols, not a technical encryption architecture. Keep the exact encryption name and retention limit fully visible.

slides.headline: New Mobility, An Old Trust Question
slides.subheadline: Ring’s new privacy promises arrive against a documented record of security failures.

metrics.label: FTC investigation year

metrics.label: US customers’ accounts accessed by hackers
metrics.body: The FTC attributed this access to Ring’s lackluster safeguards.
